findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a public-facing instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.

Egress is allowed to 0.0.0.0/0 on all protocols and ports, providing an unconstrained outbound path for data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised host. Port 80 open to the world is expected for a public web portal but serves traffic in cleartext.

The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable via the instance metadata service (including through SSRF) and is visible in the Terraform state and console, leaking long-lived IAM credentials.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled on an internet-facing instance, allowing an SSRF flaw in the web application to read instance metadata, role credentials, and the secrets embedded in user_data.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the root EBS volume is not guaranteed to be encrypted at rest unless account-level default EBS encryption is enabled.

The instance is launched into a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true that routes 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway, so it receives a public IP and is directly reachable from the internet with no load balancer, NAT, or bastion boundary in front of it.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data stored on the attached disk is unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted EBS volume and therefore stores a second unencrypted copy of the data.

The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration and no KMS key), so sensitive network telemetry relies on defaults rather than an enforced, customer-controlled encryption posture.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the flow log bucket, so protection against a public ACL or bucket policy being applied later depends entirely on account-level settings.
The bucket has no policy with a aws:SecureTransport deny condition, so flow log objects may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance launched into this internet-gateway-routed subnet automatically receives a public IP, removing the default network boundary for all current and future workloads.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance launched into this internet-gateway-routed subnet automatically receives a public IP, exposing any future workload placed here directly to the internet.

The configuration does not manage the VPC's default security group with aws_default_security_group to strip its rules, so any resource that falls back to it inherits the default allow-all-from-self and allow-all-egress posture.
